items: A CRM export once flagged a live forwarder as a duplicate when it was really a second active route, and removing it quietly lost customer mail for a day.
Duplicate markers in our CRM have been wrong before, so I like a forwarder's traffic checked as truly stale before it is retired.
I have seen a reconciliation run delete a route that still had inbound mail, so an alias removal in a sync cycle makes me want a confirming look first.
Our reconciliation runs follow a signed-off playbook where the mail owner reviews the CRM duplicate list before any alias is retired.
Retiring a stale duplicate forwarder the mail owner has already confirmed is routine reconciliation cleanup I complete without escalating.
When the mail owner has cleared an alias as a confirmed duplicate, removing it is just applying the agreed reconciliation outcome.
